messages.subject: WORKSHOPS: Distance sampling training, Tanzania
parts:
Dear distance-sampling list,

Registration is now open for workshops in practical skills for
ecologists to be held in Arusha, Tanzania, between 9th and 24th June. A summary
of the workshops are given below; more information is available at
http://www.tzcrc.org/skills/ Please direct any questions to
arushaskill...@gmail.com

The workshops are linked to the 2011 International Joint Meeting of the
Association for Tropical Biology and Society for Conservation Biology, to be
held in Arusha from 12-16th June. http://www.atbc-scbafrica2011.org/

Workshops:

Primer on Distance Sampling
6-8 June
The emphasis of the workshop will be on how to design a good survey, how to
collect good data and how to do preliminary analyses using pen and paper, a
calculator and a computer spreadsheet.
Target audience: Any wildlife biologist who wants to design, collect or analyze
distance sampling survey data. Complete beginners are very welcome. Those with
more experience may: (i) benefit from the refresher, (ii) learn something from
the detailed discussion of assumptions, how to meet them, and what happens if
things go wrong, (iii) be able to use the material as a basis for teaching others.
Cost US$150

Distance Sampling Survey Design and Analysis
9-11 June
This workshop will focus on how to analyze distance sampling data in the
software Distance, as well as covering more advanced aspects of survey design.
Target audience: People who are familiar with the concepts covered on the
previous workshop, and who want to analyze survey data using the program
Distance. Pre-requisites: Attendance at workshop 1, or familiarity with all of
the concepts covered on that workshop (see web site for details).
US$150

Introduction to GIS
9-11 June
Elements of GIS, creation of maps & integration of GPS data, spatial analysis.
Focusing on QGIS (a free GIS package), this 3 day course will give practical
skills in creating maps, understanding cartographic concepts, and basic analysis.
US$100 for sponsored attendees, US$30 for unfunded students.

Introduction to GIS (Repeat of above course)
17-19 June
As above

Introduction to statistical analysis with R
20-24 June
This course offers students the chance to learn basic statistical methods at the
same time as learning R. The course aims to give students confidence in their
ability to undertake basic statistical analysis, give an awareness of the ways
in which these models can be extended, and to provide basic competence in using R.
US$100 for sponsored attendees, $30 for unfunded students.

--
Len Thomas, Co-ordinator, Distance Development Project
